([[Bradenton, Florida]]) | draft_year = 2020 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 52 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2020 | years1 = {{nbay|2020|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team1 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years2 = [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021]] | team2 = →[[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | years3 = {{nbay|2023|start}} | team3 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team4 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years5 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team5 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years6 = 2025–present | team6 = [[Ningbo Rockets]] | highlights = * NBA G League All-Rookie Team ([[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021]]) }} '''Kenyon Lee''' "'''KJ'''" '''Martin Jr.''' (born January 6, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Ningbo Rockets]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). The son of former NBA player [[Kenyon Martin]], he grew up in southern California and played basketball while attending [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (California)|Chaminade College Prep]] and [[Sierra Canyon School|Sierra Canyon]] before going to [[IMG Academy]] for his [[postgraduate year]]. He was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the second round of the [[2020 NBA draft]]. In November 2020, the Kings traded Martin to the [[Houston Rockets]], where he played for three seasons. During the 2023 off-season, he was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. In November 2023, after just 2 games with the Clippers, he was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers; in February 2025 he was traded to the Detroit Pistons, who then immediately sent him to Utah. ==High school career== Kenyon Martin Jr attended [[Oaks Christian School]] as a freshman but did not play basketball that year. Early in the school year, Kenyon Martin Jr was pulled out of Oaks Christian to be homeschooled. After his freshman year, he was enrolled in [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (California)|Chaminade College Preparatory]] where he started playing basketball as a sophomore.{{Cite web|date=June 12, 2017|title=K.J. Martin, son of former NBA star Kenyon Martin, transfers to Sierra Canyon (Calif.)|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/k-j-martin-kenyon-martin-sierra-canyon-basketball|access-date=March 1, 2021|work=USA TODAY High School Sports}}{{Cite web|date=November 24, 2016|title=Boys' basketball: K.J. Martin, son of NBA's Kenyon Martin, is making progress at Chaminade|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-k-j-martin-son-of-nba-s-kenyon-martin-is-making-progress-at-chaminade-20161124-story.html|access-date=March 1, 2021|work=Los Angeles Times}} A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] from [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles|Chatsworth, California]], Martin played alongside [[Scotty Pippen Jr.]] and [[Cassius Stanley]]. Martin averaged 16.7 points and 9.8 rebounds per game for the back-to-back California Open Division champions.{{cite news |last1=Spears |first1=Marc |title=How Kenyon Martin is supporting his son's decision to skip college and go pro |url=https://andscape.com/features/how-kenyon-martin-is-supporting-his-sons-decision-to-skip-college-and-go-pro/ |access-date=March 27, 2020 |work=[[Andscape]] |date=July 9, 2019}} Martin originally committed to play collegiately for [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] before opting for a [[postgraduate year]] at [[IMG Academy]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/draft/2020/03/25/kenyon-martin-jr-son-kenyon-martin-nba-draft/5076656002/|title=Kenyon Martin Jr., son of former No. 1 overall pick, declares for 2020 NBA Draft|first=Chris|last=Bumbaca|website=[[USA Today]]|date=March 25, 2020|access-date=March 27, 2020}} He averaged 20 points and eight rebounds per game at IMG Academy, drawing praise for his athleticism.{{cite news |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |title=Kenyon Martin Jr., son of longtime NBA player, declares for draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28950590/kenyon-martin-jr-son-long-nba-player-declares-draft |access-date=March 27, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=March 24, 2020}} Martin scored 37 points at the National Prep Showcase and demonstrated an improved jump shot.{{cite news |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Kenyon Martin Jr. and his father discuss the professional path |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Kenyon-Martin-Jr-Kenyon-Martin-NBA-G-League-Professional-Vanderbilt-139391362/ |access-date=March 27, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=November 29, 2019}} Martin declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] on March 24, 2020.{{cite web|author=Timothy Rapp|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2882881-kenyon-martin-jr-declares-for-2020-nba-draft-will-skip-college|title=Kenyon Martin Jr. Declares for 2020 NBA Draft, Will Skip College|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=March 24, 2020|access-date=September 18, 2020}}{{cite web|author=Adrian Wojnarowski|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28950590/kenyon-martin-jr-son-long-nba-player-declares-draft|title=Kenyon Martin Jr., son of longtime NBA player, declares for draft|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=March 24, 2020|access-date=September 18, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2020–2023)=== ====2020-21==== On November 18, 2020, Martin was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the second round of the [[2020 NBA draft]] with the 52nd overall pick. On November 25, he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for cash considerations and a future second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-kj-martin-jr|title=Rockets Acquire KJ Martin Jr.|website=Nba.com|date=November 25, 2020|access-date=December 2, 2020}} Martin signed a four-year contract with the Rockets on November 30.{{cite news |last1=DoBose |first1=Ben |title=Rockets sign KJ Martin Jr. to four-year deal; first season guaranteed |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/30/rockets-sign-kj-martin-jr-to-four-year-deal-first-season-guaranteed/ |access-date=December 2, 2020 |work=Rockets Wire |date=November 30, 2020}} The Rockets organization put him on their G League affiliate team, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{Cite web|title=Kenyon Martin Jr. {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/player/1630231/kenyon_martin_jr|access-date=March 3, 2021|website=Nba.com}} Martin was activated by the Houston Rockets for the January 4, 2021, game against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], then was inactive for one game before making his on-court NBA debut on January 8, 2021, vs. the [[Orlando Magic]], scoring 7 points on 3-3 shooting (including a three-pointer){{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/martike04/gamelog/2021/|title=Kenyon Martin Jr. 2020-21 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 12, 2022}} On May 8, 2021, Martin scored a season career-high 27 points against the Utah Jazz.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202105080UTA.html|title=Houston Rockets at Utah Jazz Box Score, May 8, 2021|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 12, 2022}} He had a then-career high 10 rebounds in three different games, all in May 2021. ====2021-22==== [[File:Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Houston Rockets (51761663845).jpg|thumb|right|Martin attempts to dunk over [[Dean Wade]] of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2021]] Martin played in 79 of 82 games during the season, starting two. He scored a season-high 20 points on March 2, 2022, against the [[Utah Jazz]] and twice snared 11 rebounds in a game.{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/martike04/gamelog/2022 | title=Kenyon Martin Jr. 2021-22 Game Log }} ====2022-23==== Before the season, Martin made a trade request to the Rockets with the desire of playing more minutes. He instead became a full-time starter when Eric Gordon was traded in February 2023.{{cite news |last1=Davis |first1=Coty M. |title=Exclusive: An Unbroken Vow Helping Rockets K.J. Martin Grow Leaps and Bounds In Year 3 |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/houston-rockets-kj-martin-exclusive-career-high-stephen-silas |access-date=5 October 2023 |work=Sports Illustrated|date=30 March 2023 |language=en}} Martin played in all 82 of the Rockets' games, starting 49 of them in his third season in the NBA.{{cite web | url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/rockets-wizards-game-recap-win-season-finale-17887163.php | title=Rockets 114, Wizards 109 : Houston fights back to win season finale | date=April 9, 2023 }} He also achieved career highs in points per game (12.7), field goal percentage (.572), rebounds per game (5.5), and minutes per game (28.0).{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/martike04.html | title=Kenyon Martin Jr. Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more }} On November 25, 2022, he scored 21 points along with a career-high 15 rebounds in a 128–122 win against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |title=Stephen Silas excited by Houston's improvement on defense, rebounds |url=https://www.yahoo.com/now/stephen-silas-excited-houston-improvement-211920518.html |access-date=2022-11-27 |website=www.yahoo.com |language=en-US}} On March 22, 2023, Martin scored a career-high 31 points, shooting 12-18 from the field against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |last=Coty |first=M. Davis |date=March 23, 2023 |title=Rockets vs. Grizzlies Takeaways: K.J. Martin Motivated By Jaren Jackson Jr.'s Physicality |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/.amp/news/houston-rockets-vs-grizzlies-loss-takeaways-kj-martin-jaren-jackson-jr-ja-morant |access-date=March 23, 2023}} On February 18, 2023, he was one of four participants in the AT&T Slam Dunk Contest on all-star weekend.{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-slam-dunk-contest | title=Mac McClung steals the show, wins 2023 AT&T Slam Dunk | website=[[NBA.com]] }} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2023)=== On July 8, 2023, the Rockets traded Martin to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for two future second-round picks.{{cite web|title=LA CLIPPERS ACQUIRE KENYON MARTIN JR.|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-acquire-kenyon-martin-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2023–2025)=== On November 1, 2023, the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] acquired Martin, [[Marcus Morris Sr.]], [[Nicolas Batum]] and [[Robert Covington]] from the Clippers in exchange for [[James Harden]], [[P. J. Tucker]], and [[Filip Petrušev]]. As part of the trade, the Clippers dealt a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a pick swap, and cash considerations to the 76ers, while sending a pick swap and cash considerations to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|title=Three-Team Deal with LA Clippers, Oklahoma City Thunder Completed|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-trade-harden-tucker-to-clippers|website=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2023|access-date=November 1, 2023}} On July 15, 2024, he re-signed with the Sixers on a two-year, $16 million contract.{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Re-Sign KJ Martin|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-re-sign-kj-martin|website=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2024|access-date=July 15, 2024}} ===Utah Jazz (2025)=== On February 6, 2025, Martin and two future second-round picks (2027 via Milwaukee; 2031 via Dallas) were traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-complete-trade-with-detroit-pistons|title=Philadelphia 76ers Complete Trade With Detroit Pistons|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}} Several hours later, he was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in a five-team trade, including [[Jimmy Butler]] to the Warriors.{{cite web | title=Jimmy Butler joins Warriors in 5-team deal with Heat | website=NBA | date=2025-02-06 | url=https://www.nba.com/news/jimmy-butler-heading-to-warriors-in-multi-player-deal-with-heat | access-date=2025-12-02}} Martin made 19 appearances (nine starts) for the Jazz, averaging 6.3 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. On September 23, Martin was waived by the Jazz.{{Cite web |date=2025-09-24 |title=Should the Sixers Consider A Reunion with KJ Martin? |url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/should-the-sixers-consider-a-reunion-with-kj-martin-01k5wh24j5tt |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Philadelphia 76ers On SI |language=en-US}} === Ningbo Rockets (2025–present) === On November 15, 2025, Martin signed with the [[Ningbo Rockets]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web |title=00状元肯扬·马丁之子转战CBA！24岁火箭旧将KJ·马丁加盟宁波队 |url=https://news.zhibo8.com/nba/2025-11-15/691851133821bnative.htm |website=直播吧 |access-date=November 17, 2025 |date=November 15, 2025}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2020}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | 45 || 8 || 23.7 || .509 || .365 || .714 || 5.4 || 1.1 || .7 || '''.9''' || 9.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | 79 || 2 || 21.0 || .533 || .357 || .634 || 3.8 || 1.3 || .4 || .5 || 8.8 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | '''82''' || '''49''' || '''28.0''' || .569 || .315 || .680 || '''5.5''' || '''1.5''' || .5 || .4 || '''12.7''' |- | style="text-align:left;" rowspan=2| {{nbay|2023}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
